title: Understanding Language Models
introduction: Language models are AI systems that work with text. They help computers understand and create language, which is useful in many everyday tools.

sections.heading: What Is a Language Model?
sections.subheading: A simple definition of the AI tool
paragraphs: A language model is a computer program that learns patterns in written language. It looks at lots of text and learns how words usually appear together.

example.title: Predicting the next word in a sentence
example.content: If the model sees "The cat sat on the", it predicts the next word is likely "mat" because that phrase is common in English.

sections.heading: How Language Models Use Text Sequences
sections.subheading: Working with words as ordered tokens
paragraphs: Language models treat a sentence as a sequence of tokens, where each token can be a word or part of a word. The order of tokens matters because meaning changes with position.

example.title: Filling in a missing word
example.content: Given the sequence "She opened the ___ and saw a surprise", the model guesses "door" because "opened the door" is a frequent pattern.

sections.heading: Next‑Token Prediction Explained
sections.subheading: The core idea behind generating text
paragraphs: The model predicts the next token by calculating which word is most likely to follow the previous ones. This process repeats to create longer sentences.

example.title: Completing a story line
example.content: Starting with "Once upon a time, a brave knight", the model may continue "ventured into the dark forest" as the next phrase, based on story patterns.

sections.heading: Language Models in Everyday Life
sections.subheading: Common applications you may have seen
paragraphs: You interact with language models when you use chatbots, voice assistants, or auto‑complete on your phone. They help generate helpful responses quickly.

example.title: Chatbot answering a question
example.content: When you ask a virtual assistant "What is the weather today?", the model processes your words and generates a short answer like "It is sunny with a high of 75°F."

practice.title: Try Predicting the Next Word
practice.instruction: Write a short sentence, stop before the last word, and guess what comes next. Then check your guess by looking up the phrase online or using a free language model tool to see if your prediction matches.

keyTakeaways: A language model learns patterns in text to predict or generate words.
It works with sequences of tokens, where order influences meaning.
Next‑token prediction is the basic mechanism behind many AI applications like chatbots and auto‑complete.

mcqs.question: What is the main task of a language model?
options: Predict the next word in a sequence
mcqs.explanation: A language model learns patterns in text and is used to predict the most likely next word or token.

mcqs.question: Why does token order matter for a language model?
options: Because changing order can change meaning
mcqs.explanation: The meaning of a sentence depends on the sequence of words; rearranging tokens can produce a different meaning.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an everyday example of a language model?
options: An auto‑complete feature on a phone keyboard
mcqs.explanation: Auto‑complete suggests words as you type by predicting the next token, which is a direct use of a language model.

mcqs.question: In the sentence "She opened the ___ and saw a surprise", what word is the model most likely to fill in?
mcqs.explanation: The phrase "opened the door" is a common pattern in English, so the model predicts "door" as the most likely word.

mcqs.question: What is the term for the process where the model repeatedly predicts the next token to build longer text?
mcqs.explanation: Generating longer sentences involves repeatedly applying next‑token prediction, the core mechanism described in the lesson.
